blocks.x: Planning a business remodel before your fiscal year-end? The type of work decides how the cost is treated for tax, and the timing can affect when you get the benefit. Whether a renovation is a capital expense or a current expense changes how much you can deduct this year.

Here's a plain-language overview for Canadian business owners and landlords, about property used to earn income. It doesn't cover renovations to your own home. This is general information, not tax advice, so always confirm your situation with your accountant.
Renovations: current expense or capital expenditure?
The Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) treats renovation costs in one of two ways:

head: Current expense
Capital expenditure
rows: Repairs that restore something to its original condition
Improvements that give a lasting benefit or make the property better than before
Painting the exterior of a wooden house, repairing wooden steps
Putting vinyl siding on a wooden house, replacing wooden steps with concrete steps
Repainting, patching drywall, fixing a leak, replacing a few broken tiles

A new [addition](/services/home-additions), a [kitchen](/services/kitchen-renovations) or [bathroom](/services/bathroom-renovations) remodel that makes the space better than before, new windows that upgrade the building
Generally deducted in the year incurred
Generally deducted over time through capital cost allowance (CCA)

blocks.x: The line isn't always obvious. A useful question is whether the work restores or betters the property.

The CRA's rental income guide uses four tests: whether the expense gives a lasting benefit, whether it maintains or improves the property, whether it's for a part of the property or a separate asset, and its value relative to the property, which isn't decisive on its own.
Capital cost allowance basics
Capital improvements are added to a CCA class and deducted gradually. Classes that can apply to renovation work include:
**Class 1:** most buildings acquired after 1987, unless they belong in another class
**Class 13:** many capital improvements a tenant makes to leased property (the maximum rate depends on the type of leasehold interest and the terms of the lease, so ask your accountant)
**Class 8:** furniture, household appliances, some fixtures and machinery
Rules for the first-year deduction have changed several times in recent years, so ask your accountant which rules apply to work completed this year.
Year-end timing tips
**Know your fiscal year-end.** Current expenses are generally deducted in the year you incur them, so work completed before year-end may count this year.
**Schedule true repairs before year-end** if you want the deduction this year.
**Document the scope clearly.** An invoice that separates repairs from improvements makes the tax treatment easier to support.

**Claim GST input tax credits where you can.** If you're a GST registrant, you can generally recover the GST paid on renovations related to your commercial activities, including commercial rentals. Long-term residential rents (one month or more) are exempt, so you generally can't claim credits on costs for those units. Capital real property has its own rules.

**Treat Manitoba Retail Sales Tax (RST) separately.** Input tax credits recover GST, not RST. On construction, installation, maintenance or repair of real property, Manitoba Finance says contractors pay RST on their materials and should not charge it on their billings. Other goods and work can be taxed differently, so ask your accountant.

**Check rebates first.** Some energy incentives require approval before work starts, as [Efficiency Manitoba's Building Envelope Program](https://efficiencymb.ca/business/building-envelope/) does. Missing that step can cost you the incentive.
For rental property owners

The CRA encourages landlords to report rental income and expenses on Form T776. The same test applies: work that restores a unit to its original condition is usually a current expense, and work that makes it better than before is usually capital.
Repairs that put a used property you just acquired into suitable condition for use are capital. You can't use CCA to create or increase a rental loss.
Keep these records
Contracts and detailed invoices showing scope
Proof of payment
Before-and-after photos
Permits and inspection records
Rebate approvals and payments, because the CRA has you subtract a rebate from the related cost
The bottom line
Year-end renovations can be well timed for tax, as long as the work is properly classified and documented. Plan with your accountant, then book the work.
